topics.title: The AI wage premium just hit 62% — but only for four specific skills
topics.why: PwC's 2026 Global AI Jobs Barometer shows the premium is concentrated in LangChain, RAG, vector databases, and multi-agent orchestration, not "AI" broadly — a sharper, more actionable read than the generic wage-premium headline.

topics.title: Handshake AI and Transfyr are paying degreed professionals to fix AI models — deadlines are this month
topics.why: Two fellowship programs recruiting lawyers, scientists, and PhDs into paid model-evaluation work have application windows closing in August 2026, making this a time-boxed opportunity rather than evergreen advice.

topics.title: UK data shows a real two-speed jobs market — and it's not the bifurcation you'd expect
topics.why: Indeed's new UK figures show AI-skilled hiring rising even as overall postings fall about 10% from last year, giving the "bifurcation" story an actual number instead of a vibe.

topics.title: AI job titles have tripled since 2022 — most of them aren't engineering roles
topics.why: New labor-market data show AI-labeled postings growing fastest in sales, education, and management, meaning the fastest-growing "AI job" category doesn't require a CS background — worth mapping who's actually getting hired.

topics.title: Tech and finance are losing 28,000 jobs a month — here's what's actually replacing them
topics.why: New payroll data show accelerating losses concentrated in the sectors adopting AI fastest, but the same data hints at where those workers are landing next — a more useful frame than another "AI is coming for jobs" headline.
